problems: All 12 findings of the review that were not marked applied were worked: Iraq 1946-1947, Iraq 1920-1921, Senegal, Dominica and Saint Vincent, Martinique and Guadeloupe, Guyana, New France, the 1796/1819/1842 boundary events, Manila, the Mosquito Coast, Arakan and Tenasserim, and the 1709/1713 hand-over. British counterpart convention still open: the same events are named differently by other authors (kingdom-of-iraq names kingdom-of-great-britain for the 1921-1932 and 1941-1947 occupations; burma names british-empire for Arakan and Tenasserim; new-france and the Guiana dossiers name british-colonial-empire). This row names the other party (kingdom-of-iraq, burma, new-france, batavian-republic) so that each event mirrors, but the orchestrator should fix one British counterpart per period.

Mosquito Coast: TE has a continuous protectorate in two rows (1668-1786, 1787-1861); the Mosquito Coast page ends it in 1787, records recognition of independence in 1837 and a new protectorate in 1844. The dossier follows TE for 1787-1843 at confidence 2; the mosquito-kingdom dossier (found 1844) has no vassal events.

Iraq: the review offered an occupation or a keyframe correction; both were done. The 1920-1921 shape keeps Iraq as direct land until the Kingdom's founding on 23 August 1921 and the mandate is carried as an occupation (as in kingdom-of-iraq), not a vassal. The 1946 shape now drops Iraq, Jordan, Israel, Palestine, Saudi Arabia, Syria and Kuwait; Kuwait (a protectorate) is also removed from the 1915-1921 shapes.

Cliopatria's cells lag the pages (Senegal drawn from 1762 against 1758, Guyana 1797 against 1796, Réunion kept to 1819 against its 1814 return, Tenasserim 1825 against the 1826 cession); events carry the page dates. Keyframes were corrected only for Réunion 1815-1819, the English colonies 1709-1712 (double-drawn with english-colonial-empire, whose dossier hands over in 1713, now agreed) and the Middle East in 1915-1921 and 1946.

The 1819 and 1842 boundary events are below the Cliopatria grid (no shape of this row changes then); the 1796 event is corroborated by the shape (Detroit cells 8 to 2). Three pages did not load (url_not_found) and were not retried; the Saint-Louis and Réunion pages carry the Senegal and Réunion dates instead.
